title: Drive a circuit: laps through checkpoints against a clock
summary: One vehicle on a road loop built from data, checkpoints in order make a lap, N laps before the clock runs out. Covers time trials, kart circuits, delivery runs with gates, slaloms.
applies_when: the player drives a vehicle along a road or course that closes into a loop or runs between gates
progress is passing checkpoints in order, and winning is laps or gates inside a time limit
pickups or pads on the road give a boost, and loose obstacles may be knocked over
not_when: several cars race each other for position (the seed has no opponent; a pace car by TLSteer.keep_lane is possible but ranking is not shown)
the vehicle leaves the road for open terrain or stunts

data_files.role: the venue: one circuits[] entry whose control points are the road; the built road node carries its centre line, length and half width
laps to win, number of checkpoints, the time limit
start place and checkpoint places as shares of the lap, cone places, every vehicle tuning member

do: Place everything by distance along the centre line (s metres along, off metres to the side): start, checkpoints, pads, cones. Then moving the road moves the game.
Make each checkpoint a trigger across the road and report it with rules.pass_checkpoint; let the rules count laps.
Pass the vehicle tuning dictionary from JSON straight into TLVehicle.create; drive it with drive_from_input and an action map.
Use a spawner for anything that should come back (cones, pickups) and let its jitter draw from the seeded generator.
Register the chase camera first (it is what play shows) and one fixed overview.
Keep pads and the start on a straight.
dont: Do not lay the road from boxes or planks: a circuit is data in the layout and the kit builds it.
Do not count laps or time in the script: laps_to_win, checkpoints and time_limit_seconds are the rules.
Do not place things by world coordinates copied from one layout: they break when the road changes.
Do not set the car's position or velocity to steer it: use its inputs, the same ones the bot uses.
Do not set a clock the bot cannot beat with margin: measure the bot's time first, then set the limit about half as long again.

bot.plays_by: the player's own actions only: it steers toward a point ahead on the centre line (TLSteer.keep_lane), slows when the far point swings sideways, and uses nitro on straights.
bot.wins_when: the rules say state over, winner car, reason laps with the full lap count; a finish by reason time fails.

acceptance: The bot completes every lap with reason laps, never time, at seeds 1 and 2.
A car that does not move loses by time.
Checkpoints only count in order: driving the loop backwards completes no lap.
Lint reports 0 bypasses and 0 kit parts added.
The chase camera keeps the car in frame for the whole bot run and the HUD shows lap and clock.

variants.change: one number each in rules.json; re-measure the bot before tightening the clock.
move the control points in track.json; checkpoints, cones and the start follow because they are placed by s.
more checkpoints as narrow triggers, cones from the spawner beside each gate.
the road's surface in the layout: grip follows from the law table (asphalt 1.0 against ice 0.1), so lower the bot's cornering speed with it.
